text.p: The following are some of the leading stories and commentary in Finnish papers this morning dealing with Finland's decision to link the markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism, ERM.

- Decision to peg markka to ERM is not expected to shake financial and foreign exchange markets. ERM linkage at 3.04 markka to the Deutschemark was close to the average for central parity rates over the past two years. @
- Decision to join ERM was government show of strength just a week ahead of local government and European parliament elections -- editorial comment.
- Time now for Finland to begin discussion of joining EMU, due for start-up in just over 500 business days, writes editor Janne Virkkunen.
- Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen said central parity exchange rate is an equilibrium rate, and she did not expect the bank to intervene to defend the markka at that rate. @
- Markka-ERM link perhaps more to do with security policy than economic issues, writes Atte Jaaskalainen.
- Finland's ERM link took Sweden by surprise -- initial Swedish reaction cautious.
- Finland wanted to join ERM before Italy: "We don't want our economic reputation confused with Italy," an unnamed minister said.
- Industry and organised labour approve linkage rate. @
- Politically, decision on whether to proceed to monetary union likely to be thorny, as main opposition Centre Party is highly critical -- editorial.
- By tying the markka, Finland daintily says "I do" to Europe's macho man, the Euro, writes Kari Ikonen.

- ERM link is a double-edged sword: it can boost credibility of economic policy but also can wake speculators. Markets could test whether there is a tighter fluctuation band within the official one, Finland Bank economist Sinimaaria Ranki said. @
- Finland, by detaching itself from neighbouring Sweden through ERM link, has lifted itself closer to the European core than Sweden -- editorial.
- Finland's representative to the European monetary committee Johnny Akerholm said Brussels meeting on ERM link went smoothly, without any disagreements.
